title: Geometric decay of a shrinking weight sequence
statement:
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a real number $\beta$ with $0 < \beta < 1$, and let $W \colon \bbn \to \bbr$ be a sequence of strictly positive reals with $W(0) = n$. Suppose that for every $k < M$ the sequence shrinks by at least the factor $(1+\beta)/2$ at each step, in the sense that
\[
  W(k+1) \;\le\; W(k)\cdot\frac{1+\beta}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; n\left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive integer (0 < n)
W(k+1) ≤ W(k)·((1+β)/2) for all k < M
replaced:
Under the same shrinkage hypothesis as \texttt{wm\_weight\_shrinkage}, if additionally
$n \ge 1$ and the initial total weight satisfies $W(0) = n$, then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; n \cdot \left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
